title: Flight training: First Light
intro: Training run. Fly to the storm and the fire, point an instrument at each, then send what you saw home through a relay satellite. Nothing here changes your mission score.
complete_text: Training complete. You observed, stored and sent data, which is the same job every Earth-watching satellite does every day.

targets.label: Hurricane

feedback.approach: Hurricane ahead. Point a camera at the eye and hold steady.
feedback.done: Got it. Pictures show where the storm is and how big it is.
feedback.partial: Observed, but you have no camera or imager on board. Next time, add one to see clouds and storms clearly.

targets.fact: NASA's MODIS cameras on Terra and Aqua see the whole Earth every 1 to 2 days, in 36 colors of light.

targets.label: Wildfire

feedback.approach: Smoke below. Infrared sees the heat through it. Hold steady over the fire.
feedback.done: Hot spot found. Infrared shows the fire's edge even under smoke.
feedback.partial: Observed, but only smoke shows up. An infrared spectrometer or multispectral imager would see the fire's heat.

targets.fact: NASA's FIRMS service sends satellite fire detections to firefighters worldwide within 3 hours of the satellite passing over.

targets.label: TDRS relay satellite

feedback.approach: Relay satellite in range. Point your antenna at it to send your data home.
feedback.done: Data sent. The relay passes it down to the ground, so scientists see it in minutes.
feedback.blocked: Nothing to send yet. Observe the hurricane and the wildfire first.

targets.fact: NASA's TDRS relay satellites sit in geosynchronous orbit and relay data for more than 25 missions, including Hubble and the Space Station.
